geo:GSE308434.title: Tumor-intrinsic and extrinsic immune mechanisms define resistance to immune checkpoint blockade in metastatic melanoma [snRNA]
geo:GSE308434.study_title: Tumor-intrinsic and extrinsic immune mechanisms define resistance to immune checkpoint blockade in metastatic melanoma [snRNA]
geo:GSE308434.notes: resp_score=0; gdstype=Expression profiling by high throughput sequencing
geo:GSE308434.description: The interplay between variable genomic, transcriptional, and microenvironmental features driving resistance to immune checkpoint blockade (ICB) remains poorly understood. Here, we performed multi-omic profiling (single-nucleus RNA, T cell receptor, and whole-genome sequencing) of 42 sequential biopsies from 34 patients with metastatic melanoma. Using a Bayesian integrative model, we identify recurring features of ICB-sensitive and resistant clones, and uncouple gene dosage effects from transcriptional output, thereby defining genetic and non-genetic basis for plasticity. Joint characterization of tumor-immune microenvironment uncovered evolution of malignant and immune cells with ICB treatment, capturing clinically relevant shifts in T cell states and macrophage polarization. Co-evolving crosstalk among malignant and immune compartments defined clone‑specific immune‑evasion circuits, including erosion of the CD58-CD2 axis. This study provides a unified framework for disentangling complex intra- and inter-cellular genotype-phenotype interactions, and shows that evolving immune dysfunction ensues upon prolonged exposure to ICB, thus informing clinical practice in melanoma and beyond.

geo:GSE320041.title: High-resolution and noninvasive profiling of the tumor microenvironment with spatial ecotypes [Visium]
geo:GSE320041.study_title: High-resolution and noninvasive profiling of the tumor microenvironment with spatial ecotypes [Visium]
geo:GSE320041.description: Multicellular programs in the tumor microenvironment (TME) drive cancer pathogenesis and response to therapy but remain challenging to identify and profile clinically. Here, we present a machine learning framework for multi-analyte profiling of spatially dependent cell states and multicellular ecosystems, termed spatial ecotypes (SEs). By integrating 10M single-cell and spot-level spatial transcriptomes from diverse human carcinomas and melanomas, we identified nine SEs with broad conservation—each with unique biology, geospatial features, and clinical outcome associations, including several linked to immunotherapy response. Notably, SEs were distinguishable by DNA methylation profiling and recoverable from plasma cell-free DNA (cfDNA) using deep learning. In cfDNA from nearly 100 melanoma patients, SE levels exhibited striking associations with immunotherapy response. Our data reveal fundamental units of TME organization and demonstrate a multimodal platform for solid and liquid TME profiling, with implications for improved risk stratification and therapy personalization.

geo:GSE324265.title: Contribution of cytotoxic CD8 T cells, neutrophils and type 1 interferon signaling to hyperinflammatory pathology in HIV associated TB meningitis [RNA-Seq]
geo:GSE324265.study_title: Contribution of cytotoxic CD8 T cells, neutrophils and type 1 interferon signaling to hyperinflammatory pathology in HIV associated TB meningitis [RNA-Seq]
geo:GSE324265.notes: resp_score=0; gdstype=Expression profiling by high throughput sequencing
geo:GSE324265.description: Immune dysregulation contributes to death and disability in tuberculous meningitis. People living with HIV have the highest risk of TBM, greatest death and disability, and the least evidence that anti-inflammatory therapy improves the poor outcome. Improving therapy relies on a more refined understanding of the host immune response. Using single-cell RNA sequencing, we characterised 188,983 lumbar CSF cells from 25 adults with HIV-associated TBM and identified correlates of bacterial load. There was heterogeneity in cell composition between patients, but cytotoxic CD8 T cells with low cytokine expression were consistently predominant with a large number expressing GZMK, known to activate complement. In microbiologically-confirmed TBM, there was greater cytotoxicity in T, NK and γδ cells, and higher type 1 interferon stimulation in T and B lymphocytes. Neutrophils expressed markers suggesting heightened cytokine stimulation, enhanced effector function, and IL-8-mediated peripheral neutrophil recruitment. In a separate longitudinal cohort, type 1 interferon signalling increased in the blood and CSF following treatment initiation. Overall, findings indicate a hyper-inflammatory immune response in the CSF of HIV-associated TBM patients characterised by an accumulation of granzyme-rich cytotoxic CD8 T cells, highly activated neutrophils and host-detrimental type 1 IFN signalling.

geo:GSE328575.notes: resp_score=0; gdstype=Expression profiling by high throughput sequencing
geo:GSE328575.description: This dataset profiles intra-tumor heterogeneity in renal cell carcinoma using single-cell gene expression analysis. Single-cell transcriptomic profiles were generated to characterize malignant and non-malignant cell populations and to enable comparative analyses between primary and metastatic disease states. Gene expression data were used to derive gene programs that capture transcriptional heterogeneity among renal cell carcinoma cells.

geo:GSE328575.overall_design: Single-cell RNA sequencing was performed on 21 renal cell carcinoma specimens using the 10x Genomics platform. The cohort includes four major renal cell carcinoma subtypes: 16 clear cell renal cell carcinomas, 2 papillary renal cell carcinomas, 1 chromophobe renal cell carcinoma, 1 clear cell papillary renal cell tumor, and 1 unclassified case. Samples include 12 primary tumors and 9 metastatic tumors, derived from 16 patient tumors and 5 patientâderived xenograft models originating from primary sites or metastases to the brain and lung.  *************************************************************** Raw files for human/patient samples are being made available in EGA (https://www.ebi.ac.uk/ega/) for controlled access to the personally identifiable sequence data. ***************************************************************
